items.stem: A beginner insists they cannot start learning AI until they have mastered advanced mathematics. Why is this a weak starting assumption?

options.text: Much useful AI learning and tool use starts well before advanced maths; depth can be built as goals require
options.rationale: Correct: a goal-driven path lets you learn maths as needed rather than front-loading all of it.

options.text: Maths is never useful for AI
options.rationale: Overstated: maths matters for depth; it just need not block the start.

options.text: Only people with degrees can learn AI
Advanced maths guarantees AI expertise by itself
options.rationale: Inaccurate: practice and application are also needed.

items.explanation: Correct: a goal-driven path lets you learn maths as needed rather than front-loading all of it.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a self-directed AI learning plan more effective? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Building small projects and evaluating the results, not just consuming material
options.rationale: Correct: applied, evaluated practice builds durable skill.

options.text: Tracing bold claims back to primary sources before trusting them
options.rationale: Correct: source-checking keeps your knowledge honest in a hype-heavy field.

options.text: Memorising every new model name as it is announced
options.rationale: Low value: names change fast and rarely build skill.

options.text: Avoiding all projects until you have finished every course

items.explanation: Correct: applied, evaluated practice builds durable skill.

items.stem: Why should a learner treat a single tutorial as a starting point rather than the current state of the field?

options.text: AI moves quickly, so any one resource can be partial or out of date and should be cross-checked
options.rationale: Correct: breadth and recency require consulting multiple, current sources.
Overstated: tutorials are useful but limited in scope and freshness.
Inaccurate: format does not determine currency or accuracy.

options.text: The newest tutorial is always complete
options.rationale: Inaccurate: recency does not guarantee completeness.

items.explanation: Correct: breadth and recency require consulting multiple, current sources.
